notes: Merged 'Andrew W. Mellon Foundation' and 'Mellon Foundation' into one row named 'Mellon Foundation' (legal name: The Andrew W. Mellon Foundation, EIN 13-1879954).

Figures come from IRS data via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer (pulled 2026-11-22). Private foundations use the 990-PF fair market value of all assets at end of year; public charities and community foundations use Form 990 total assets at end of year. These are total assets, not strictly endowments.

Corporations and banks (Amazon Literary Partnership, PECO, PNC, TD Bank) have a null endowment by design. Corporate foundations (Estée Lauder, Wells Fargo) show their foundation's own 990-PF assets, which are small pass-through balances.

Name and entity notes (display names kept as given): Doris Duke Foundation was renamed from Doris Duke Charitable Foundation in 2023 (filer EIN 82-3691183). JPB Foundation has since been renamed Freedom Together Foundation. Prebys Foundation's legal name is Conrad Prebys Foundation. Kapor Foundation files as Mitchell Kapor Foundation. Donaghue Foundation is the Patrick and Catherine Weldon Donaghue Medical Research Foundation. Dana Foundation is The Charles A. Dana Foundation. Laurie M. Tisch Illumination Fund files as The Laurie M. Tisch Foundation Inc. Bloomberg Philanthropies' assets are those of the Bloomberg Family Foundation.

Gates: the figure is the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation Trust, which holds the endowment ($75.5B at 12/31/2023). The grantmaking entity (Gates Foundation, EIN 56-2618866) reports $76.95B, mostly its interest in the Trust, so do not add them.
Open Society: only the Foundation to Promote Open Society ($10.5B) is used. Open Society Institute separately reports $5.27B, but money moves between the entities, so summing them is unreliable.
Art-endowed foundations (Frankenthaler, Joan Mitchell, de Kooning, Warhol, Rauschenberg, Gottlieb) include artworks at fair market value, so they look larger than their investment endowments.
Figures older than FY2023: Lenfest Foundation (FY ending June 2022; a spend-down foundation, about $3.8M) and Mertz Gilmore Foundation (FY2022). ProPublica has no 2023 filings for either.
Duke Endowment uses its audited total assets ($4.94B at 12/31/2023) because the latest 990-PF in ProPublica's extract is FY2022.

Null endowments: Aliad Fund (a donor fund held at the Boston Foundation). Decolonizing Wealth Project (fiscally sponsored; no 990 of its own found). Jennifer and Jonathan Allan Soros, and Jon Stryker and Slobodan Randjelović (individuals; Stryker's Arcus Foundation reported $275M in 2023 but is not used). Joan Ganz Cooney & Holly Peterson Fund. Kenneth C. Griffin Charitable Fund (likely donor-advised, no public filings). Stavros Niarchos Foundation (non-US foundation with offices in Athens and New York; no official asset figure found, and a secondary list's undated ~$12B was not used). Victory Foundation (several unrelated US entities share the name, so type is also null).
Entities matched by name only (verify if important): Arnhold Foundation Inc (New York), Aviv Foundation Inc (Washington DC), Walder Family Foundation (Skokie IL), taken to be the Walder Foundation.

website_checked=true means the homepage responded to a live request, or it appeared as the official result in search. Some sites returned 403/406 bot-blocking codes but resolved on the official domain. Not checked: PNC (pnc.com did not respond to the automated check). Griffin Charitable Fund, Joan Ganz Cooney & Holly Peterson Fund).
